title: Defense Nuclear Agency records on Shockwave, 1977-1986

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Defense Nuclear Agency records on Shockwave, 1977-1986
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I request Defense Nuclear Agency records (now held by the Defense Threat Reduction Agency) on "Shockwave" (also "Shock Wave"), a theater nuclear force threat-monitoring effort in the NATO Central Region from about 1978 to 1985, described in the Defense Science Board report "Assessment of Nuclear Monitoring and Verification Technologies" (2014, pages 69–73), which names the Defense Nuclear Agency as a major participant. I request program plans, briefings, histories, after-action reports and assessments of Shockwave, including records on NATO exercises planned to elicit Warsaw Pact responses observable by Shockwave assets, dated 1977 through 1986. Please include a search of the DTRA history office files.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brian Mills

title: Defense Science Board 2011 task force briefings (Shockwave, SORAK)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Defense Science Board 2011 task force briefings (Shockwave, SORAK)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I request the briefing materials and papers presented to the Defense Science Board Task Force on Assessment of Nuclear Monitoring and Verification Technologies (final report January 2014), listed in its Appendix D: "Part 5/6. Experiment, Iterate and Adapt" (March 3, 2011 and May 4, 2011) by Dr. Rich Wagner, Dr. Jim Tegnelia and Dr. Joe Braddock, and Dr. Braddock's "DOTMLPF–Theater Nuclear Forces Paper," "Adapt & Iterate Paper" and "Testing Capability Chart." I am particularly interested in material on the Cold War "Shockwave" (also "Shock Wave") and "SORAK" programs described on pages 69–73 of the report. Records may be held by the Defense Science Board office (OUSD(A&S)/OUSD(R&E)).

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.
